questions.q: What is the difference between a budget deficit and the national debt?
options: The deficit is a yearly flow, and the debt is the total stock
The debt is yearly, and the deficit is the total
The deficit only applies to trade
questions.why: Each deficit adds to the debt.

questions.q: Which deficit goes away as an economy recovers?

options: Government borrowing that reduces private investment
Too many people in a shop
questions.why: Higher interest rates can make firms invest less.

questions.q: The Office for Budget Responsibility decides the government's tax rates.
questions.why: It produces forecasts, and it doesn't set policy.

questions.q: Which makes a given national debt easier to manage?
options: Economic growth above the interest rate on the debt
questions.why: Debt then falls as a share of GDP.

questions.q: Explain why a budget deficit may be good for an economy in a recession.

ideas.label: It supports AD, as spending is above taxes
So output and jobs are higher than they'd be otherwise

questions.model: The deficit supports AD at a time when private spending is weak. Through the multiplier, this protects output and jobs.
questions.why: When others stop spending, the government can keep going.

tests.answer: It supports aggregate demand, which protects jobs and output.
